raw_response:
I’ve farmed this land a long time, so I don’t like making big changes unless I see a strong reason. On 4.5 mu in Quzhou, wheat-maize is still the safest way for me. Wheat gives me a steady base, and maize follows right after, so even if one season is only average, I still have the other. I have well irrigation, which helps, but pumping costs money, and with only two people in the household and some off-farm work, I need a plan that is reliable and not too labor-heavy.

For wheat, I will stay with improved local seed and plant in the normal early October window. I usually do better with a moderate-to-high fertilizer rate because I would rather not risk weak tillering or yellow leaves in spring. I will split nitrogen, with part as base fertilizer and part at jointing, because that has worked better on my fields than putting everything down once. I’ll irrigate around sowing if the soil is dry, then again at jointing and filling depending on rainfall. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize immediately with very little delay. The turnaround is tight, so I will keep tillage simple and use the usual hybrid maize seed. For maize, I’ll still fertilize enough to hold yield, but not excessively, because fertilizer and irrigation both cost cash. If summer rain is decent, I may only irrigate once or twice. My thinking this year is stability first: keep the full 4.5 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, use the practices that have proven themselves on my land, and avoid both under-input and unnecessary spending.
